database: PostgreSQL 18.6 on aarch64-unknown-linux-musl, compiled by gcc (Alpine 15.2.0) 15.2.0, 64-bit
pattern: Immutable content-addressed registry plus existing shared-lock deletion checks and a long GC recovery grace period.

recovery.clock: last enrollment; renewed on absent-address retry
recovery.workSource: registered models/audits addresses, including absent objects; raw/dataset discovery unchanged
recovery.bound: One row per failed object-upload attempt, coalesced per address; at most three for descriptor plus both reports.
recovery.assumption: PUT completes within the recovery window. No fencing or upload deadline; a PUT after retirement is outside the recovery guarantee.
recovery.rejectedAlternative: Fencing and bounded upload lifetime: ObjectStore has no conditional-write support and #172 is blocked.

findings.sharedReportDeletion: Shared address lock and committed-reference check on separate writer; reader grants unchanged.
findings.retryGrace: Renewed before absent-address upload; sweep-after-retry-upload regression passes.
findings.absentRecords: Retire after configured window; in-flight recovery and 23/25-hour/default/custom-window regressions pass.
findings.duplicateRuns: UNIQUE descriptor_sha256 get-or-create. Guards precede insert/reuse; first clock/receipt preserved; repeat, denied, concurrent, conflicting-claim and lost-COMMIT retries pass.
findings.codeIdentity: Separate input-generation and model-publication identities; disposable source-mutation independence probe passes.
findings.connections: Shared socket/SQLSTATE classifier; nine publisher/orphan/report combinations pass.
findings.repeatedGuard: Retained deliberately: lock before HEAD; final SQL guard protects direct callers and checks rights after HEAD.

real backend termination after insert rolls back; enrollment survives for reclamation

publisher and both orphan/report cleanup paths classify socket and SQLSTATE failures consistently

manifest pins SQL-owned datasets, supported identities, DB clock and exact object metadata

ordinary pipeline credentials cannot forge clocks or directly change immutable identities
unsupported identities, backdated extra fields and mismatched mode/key/size are refused atomically

server work oracle observes hidden writes even when one client calls a definer function
rollback restores enrollment and removes all partially inserted manifest associations

both-mode publication and repeated reuse never enroll existing objects
mismatched input versions, preregistration, dataset pins and coverage refuse before uploads

revocation during upload rolls back and preserves enrollment, never deleting bytes
